headline: 5 Ways Global Diplomacy Is Being Outsourced To The Local Chai-Wallah
body:
1. All international peace treaties are now being drafted on the back of damp paper napkins while waiting for the ginger-garlic paste to be crushed. 

2. Geopolitical summits now include a mandatory 'kettle-whistle' phase where state leaders must demonstrate their ability to negotiate the price of a cutting-chai without triggering a regional trade war. 

3. Highly sensitive nuclear de-escalation files are being kept safe under a pile of empty biscuit packets to ensure they remain 'inaccessible to failing agencies.' 

4. Foreign delegations are required to finish at least three cups of masala chai before they are allowed to discuss borders, ensuring everyone is too jittery to declare actual conflict. 

5. Every 'urgent and bad' trade deal is now concluded by a casual 'bhai, kal batayenge' (brother, we'll tell you tomorrow) policy, effectively putting global superpower demands on an indefinite waiting list.
caption: From trade wars to cutting chai—who knew global stability was just one good steep away? ☕️📈 #Diplomacy #ChaiTime #GlobalAffairs #Geopolitics (satire)
igHook: Tag the person you trust more than a world leader to handle your urgent negotiations.
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a steaming stainless steel kettle sitting on a portable stove next to a stack of handwritten documents at a bustling roadside tea stall.

sourceHeadline.title: Trump claims 'failing nation' Iran wants a deal ‘quickly and badly’, says he'll decide on US...

judgeVerdict.reasoning: While most candidates fall into the repetitive 'listicle of petty complaints' trope regarding a former president, Candidate 4 shifts the perspective to the chaotic, mundane reality of local bureaucracy and 'chai-wallah' culture. It avoids the tired, cynical institutional critique of the other candidates, opting for a culturally specific, warmer absurdity that feels structurally fresher and more grounded in a vivid, relatable setting.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses whimsical, absurdist tropes about tea-stall culture to satirize global diplomacy. It does not name any real individuals, invoke religious or caste tensions, or include identifying details in the image prompt.
